findings.classification: New conditional historical/native source observation; reachability, unique count and remedy owner unconfirmed
findings.first_failed_contract: A page returned to an empty allocator state forgets pending invalidations while its GPU source buffer is retained; later compute dispatch bounds reads by physical buffer length rather than the logical instance watermark.
trace: The native page free first decreases active count; on reaching zero the private page reset replaces its offset allocator, sets watermark to zero and clears pending tombstones, but the separately retained InstancePage source GPU buffer is not cleared there.

Native removal frees the page batch ID and source allocation. Native prepare only runs active pages, then reuses the retained page, builds per-batch metadata and uploads the new input; the source buffer is retained when existing capacity suffices and only pending clear ranges plus new input are written.

The 6533 grass adapter dispatches workgroups rounded up from the page logical capacity; its 1a5-bound WGSL binding uses the entire source buffer and the old grass shader checks physical arrayLength and valid batch_id rather than logical watermark before atomic count/output writes.

A symbolic old upload of two entries at offsets 0 and 1, followed by the final page free and a new single-entry upload at offset 0 reusing its page and batch ID, leaves offset 1 potentially containing the old valid batch ID. With old data retained, the 1024-byte minimum and 32-byte WGSL instance stride expose offset 1; one logical entry still launches 64 invocations. If that stale entry passes the new batch visibility and frustum checks, it can contribute to the new batch.
conditions: A prior actual completed upload, final-free transition, offset/page reuse, retained physical allocation and valid recycled batch ID, supported compute path and camera/visibility are required. The offset allocator implementation was not inspected; actual reuse and ordering, GPU execution and visible effect are not demonstrated.
The old grass constructor establishes nonempty GPU-cull batches, not the required lifecycle. No claim that current 95e renderer contains this defect.

findings.classification: New conditional native API source observation; caller, reachability and unique count unconfirmed
findings.first_failed_contract: The backend trait reset removes pages, allocations, pending clears and watermarks but leaves the old active_counts, so a newly added page can use the old count at the same page index.
trace: Default backend selects PagedAllocator; trait reset forwards to its reset. If called with old active entries, reset leaves their count in active_counts. The next page add appends zero at the end, but commit indexes the recreated page number, reusing the stale count; freeing its only new allocation therefore need not trigger the private page-empty reset.
conditions: Requires a trait-level reset with active allocation(s), followed by allocator reuse and a free. Bounded literal search of source_allocator/backend/batcher .reset names found no match; aliases, multiline expressions and external callers are not excluded. No application/runtime reachability established.
This is distinct from BatchBuffer::reset and from the private per-page reset performed in the stale-source candidate.
related_historical_records: Potentially related to 774 NATIVE-INITIAL05-GROUP-071 backend allocation obligations, but no same-defect historical record found in selected evidence; no alias or accepted unique count assumed.
findings.future_repair_direction: If reset is a supported native contract and still relevant, reset or reconstruct all correlated allocator accounting as one state transition and trace callers plus replacement/current ownership.
findings.acceptance_condition: A reset leaves allocation pages, pending clears, watermarks and active counts mutually coherent for supported subsequent allocation/free use.

preserved_existing_observation.trace: BatchBuffer.reset clears the three vectors and dirty indices but retains capacity; after prior growth then reset, update at an index below old capacity can index an empty vector. Historical reviewer already recorded this conditional standalone contract; caller/reach/current state open. Do not count this as a newly accepted finding.

nonfindings_and_limits: Normal BatchBuffer growth resizes three CPU vectors together, and the runner orders source update, batching, output writes, flush and page update. This does not prove all possible public mutable states, buffer creation under zero capacity, or external reset callers.
prepare.collect_inputs filters empty instance vectors before its ordinary dirty allocation route; do not claim its normal path necessarily calls PagedAllocator.alloc(0).
BatchInfo native versus wasm first-instance branches express a platform-specific native protocol; no compatibility defect follows from the branch alone.
Different aligned/minimum physical byte capacities are not evidence the three GPU runtime arrays must have identical arrayLength.
Literal reset-name navigation and lock structural inventory are bounded evidence, not exhaustive dynamic call graph, feature resolution or product validation.
open_questions: Can the recorded old application lifecycle actually empty a page, then repopulate a smaller allocation at the same offsets with a reused batch ID, with the same backing GPU source still bound? Which scheduling and camera conditions apply?
Does the offset allocator reuse the illustrative offsets and what are the actual accepted device/buffer bounds?
Are there any external or aliased callers of the PagedAllocator trait reset? Is its reuse with active allocations a supported contract?

The prepared input length narrows from usize to u32 before allocation, while the updater collects the full instance vector for upload (see linked native prepare/updater ranges). On a 64-bit host an input exceeding u32::MAX may under-allocate; actual construction, memory/device limits, nonzero page and write reach are unresolved. 059 READ-L11-455 flagged count caps generally; /root/mhr_character independently identified this precise cross-source bridge, with separate support credit and central alias reconciliation pending.
Do any currently supported implementations contain an equivalent source-lifetime or count-coherence failure? A different 95e grass implementation exists; no direct equivalence inferred.
What are the canonical owner, relationship to other recovered queue/contracts and exact duplicate disposition?
